class: An orchestrator writes clock times into status reports, review logs, briefs or handovers from memory or as an estimate of when something will happen, instead of reading the clock or a commit; the written times drift minutes to hours from reality, including into the future, and the measured expected-vs-actual numbers built on them are wrong.
mechanism: Times were typed while composing text; no step read `date` or `git log` at the moment of writing, and no check compares a written time with the clock or the commit that added it.

first_seen.evidence: row 3 close typed ~13:35 while the close commit says 12:56; row 6 close typed with +75% when the close commit 150873d3 gave +23% (meta review after row 6).

fix: Row-review R19: every clock time is read from `date` in the same step or from a commit time, with its source when it is not 'now'; an unknown time is written as 'not recorded', never estimated.

detection.note: Prose rule only. Mechanism due (second occurrence): a repo test that refuses a time in row-review.md later than the commit that added the line (git blame), and the per-row report built from a script that reads commit times.

occurrences.where: status report and four files at 09:06-09:11 IST
occurrences.evidence: times 09:20, 09:30, 09:35, 09:40, 09:45 written at 09:06-09:11 (clock 09:11:32 when the owner asked); meta review after row 9 had flagged three typed times minutes earlier

Fourth occurrence; the mechanism is still unbuilt - it is the next process item after the reference register
